question: During the in-cab inspection, what must the driver check regarding the ammeter/voltmeter gauges?
choice_a: That the gauges show the alternator and/or generator is charging, or that the warning light is off
choice_b: That the fuel gauge reads above one-quarter tank
choice_c: That the oil pressure gauge reads in the red zone
choice_d: That the speedometer needle rests at zero
explanation: The manual states to check that gauges show the alternator and/or generator is charging or that the warning light is off.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Ammeter/Voltmeter

question: What condition must the windshield meet during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: It may have minor cracks as long as they are outside the wiper sweep
choice_b: It must be clean with no illegal stickers, no obstructions, and no damage to the glass
choice_c: It must have a manufacturer sticker in the lower right corner
choice_d: It only needs to be free of ice in winter months
explanation: The manual requires the windshield to be clean with no illegal stickers, no obstructions, or damage to the glass.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Mirrors and Windshield

question: From where should mirrors be checked to confirm they are clean and adjusted properly?
choice_a: From the fuel bay
choice_b: From behind the trailer
choice_c: From the inside
choice_d: From a stepladder outside the cab
explanation: The manual states mirrors should be clean and adjusted properly from the inside.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Mirrors and Windshield

question: What must the driver check for regarding fuses during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That the vehicle has a full box of unused fuses
choice_b: That fuses are color-coded to match wiring diagrams
choice_c: That fuses are stored in the glove compartment
choice_d: That there are spare electrical fuses
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to check for spare electrical fuses.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Emergency Equipment

question: What warning devices must be checked as part of emergency equipment, per the manual?
choice_a: Three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_b: Two red flags and a single flare
choice_c: A single reflective triangle and a flashlight
choice_d: Four fusees and one reflective triangle
explanation: The manual specifies checking for three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Emergency Equipment

question: What must be checked about the fire extinguisher during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That it is red and mounted near the driver's seat
choice_b: That it is properly charged and securely mounted
choice_c: That it has a rating sticker no more than one year old
choice_d: That it is stored in the trailer, not the cab
explanation: The manual requires checking that the fire extinguisher is properly charged and securely mounted.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Emergency Equipment

question: If a vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Fail the inspection automatically
choice_b: Install temporary fuses before continuing
choice_c: Mention this to the examiner
choice_d: Skip the emergency equipment check entirely
explanation: The manual notes that if the vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, the driver must mention this to the examiner.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Emergency Equipment (Note)

question: What must be checked about the wiper arms and blades during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That they are a matched brand-name set
choice_b: That they are replaced every six months
choice_c: That they are painted black
choice_d: That they are secure, not damaged, and operate smoothly
explanation: The manual requires checking that wiper arms and blades are secure, not damaged, and operate smoothly.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Wipers/Washers

question: Which of the following dash indicators must be tested by turning on the corresponding lights?
choice_a: Left turn signal, right turn signal, four-way emergency flashers, high beam headlight, and the ABS indicator
choice_b: Only the fuel gauge indicator
choice_c: Only the oil pressure indicator
choice_d: Only the parking brake indicator
explanation: The manual lists testing that dash indicators work when the left turn signal, right turn signal, four-way flashers, high beam headlight, and ABS indicator are turned on.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Lights/Reflectors/Reflector Tape Condition

question: What color should clearance lights display, according to the manual?
choice_a: Blue on the rear, white elsewhere
choice_b: Red on the rear, amber elsewhere
choice_c: Green on the rear, blue elsewhere
choice_d: White on the rear, red elsewhere
explanation: The manual specifies clearance lights should be red on the rear and amber elsewhere.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Lights/Reflectors/Reflector Tape Condition

question: According to the manual's note on lights, which functions must be checked separately rather than together?
choice_a: Headlight high and low beam functions
choice_b: Ammeter and voltmeter functions
choice_c: Brake, turn signal, and four-way flasher functions
choice_d: Wiper and washer functions
explanation: The manual's note states that checks of brake, turn signal, and four-way flasher functions must be done separately.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Lights/Reflectors/Reflector Tape Condition (Note)

question: What must be checked regarding the horn during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That it is louder than 90 decibels
choice_b: That it is mounted behind the grille
choice_c: That it activates automatically at intersections
choice_d: That the air horn and/or electric horn work
explanation: The manual requires checking that the air horn and/or electric horn work.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Horn

question: What must be tested regarding the heater and defroster during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That the heater and defroster work
choice_b: That the heater reaches a specific temperature within one minute
choice_c: That the defroster only operates when the engine is above idle
choice_d: That the heater is disconnected when not in use
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to test that the heater and defroster work.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Heater/Defroster

question: With air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged (trailer brakes released on combination vehicles), how does the driver check that the parking brake holds the vehicle?
choice_a: By accelerating hard in reverse
choice_b: By gently trying to pull forward with the parking brake on
choice_c: By shutting off the engine and coasting downhill
choice_d: By releasing the service brake and applying full throttle
explanation: The manual states the driver should gently try to pull the vehicle forward with the parking brake on to check that it holds.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Parking Brake Check

question: With air pressure built to governor cutout, the parking brake released, and the trailer parking brake engaged, how is the trailer parking brake checked on a combination vehicle?
choice_a: By disconnecting the glad hands and observing air loss
choice_b: By backing up rapidly
choice_c: By gently trying to pull forward with the trailer parking brake on
choice_d: By applying the service brake pedal only
explanation: The manual states the driver should gently try to pull forward with the trailer parking brake engaged to confirm it holds the vehicle.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Parking Brake Check

question: In the hydraulic brake check procedure, what should happen to the brake pedal after it is pumped three times and held down for five seconds?
choice_a: It should slowly sink to the floor
choice_b: It should bounce back up on its own
choice_c: It should feel spongy but functional
choice_d: It should not move (depress) during the five seconds
explanation: The manual states the brake pedal should not move (depress) during the five seconds it is held down.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: If equipped with a hydraulic brake reserve (back-up) system, what should the driver do with the key off?
choice_a: Depress the brake pedal and listen for the sound of the reserve system electric motor
choice_b: Remove the battery and check voltage
choice_c: Pump the accelerator pedal five times
choice_d: Disconnect the brake lines to test pressure
explanation: The manual states that with the key off, the driver should depress the brake pedal and listen for the sound of the reserve system electric motor.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: During the hydraulic brake reserve system check, what must the driver confirm about the warning buzzer or light?
choice_a: That it flashes continuously
choice_b: That it is off
choice_c: That it is louder than the horn
choice_d: That it activates only above 30 mph
explanation: The manual requires checking that the warning buzzer or light is off.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What happens if a driver fails to correctly perform all three components of the air brake check?
choice_a: The driver receives a warning and may retest immediately
choice_b: A two-point deduction is applied, but testing continues
choice_c: It results in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test
choice_d: The examiner completes the check on the driver's behalf
explanation: The manual states that failure to perform all three components of the air brake check correctly results in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check

question: In the air brake check, to what psi range is air pressure built before shutting off the engine to begin the inspection?
choice_d: 120-140 psi (governor cutoff)
explanation: The manual specifies building air pressure to governor cutoff, at 120-140 psi, before shutting off the engine.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check, Step 1

question: After fully applying the foot brake during step one of the air brake check, how long must the driver hold the brake while watching the air gauge?
choice_a: One minute
choice_b: Thirty seconds
choice_c: Five minutes
choice_d: Two minutes
explanation: The manual instructs holding the foot brake for one minute and checking the air gauge for the pressure drop.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check, Step 1

question: During the one-minute air brake hold, what is the maximum allowable pressure drop for a single vehicle?
choice_a: One pound
choice_b: Three pounds
choice_c: Four pounds
choice_d: Six pounds
explanation: The manual states the air pressure must not drop more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check, Step 1

question: During the one-minute air brake hold, what is the maximum allowable pressure drop for a combination vehicle?
choice_a: Two pounds
choice_b: Three pounds
choice_c: Four pounds
choice_d: Five pounds
explanation: The manual states the air pressure must not drop more than four pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check, Step 1

question: While fanning off air pressure in step two of the air brake check, before what psi level should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, flag) activate?
choice_a: 90 psi
choice_b: 75 psi
choice_c: 65 psi
choice_d: 55 psi
explanation: The manual states low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check, Step 2

question: Continuing to fan off air pressure on a tractor-trailer combination, at approximately what psi should the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close ("pop out")?
choice_a: Approximately 40 psi
choice_b: Approximately 100 psi
choice_c: Approximately 10 psi
choice_d: Approximately 70 psi
explanation: The manual states that at approximately 40 psi on a tractor-trailer combination, the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out).
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Air Brake Check, Step 3

question: During the service brake check, at approximately what speed should the driver pull forward before applying the service brake?
choice_a: 15 mph
choice_b: 5 mph
choice_c: 25 mph
choice_d: 35 mph
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake, and stop.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Service Brake Check

question: What is the service brake check designed to determine?
choice_a: That the vehicle's fuel economy is unaffected by braking
choice_b: That the parking brake can be disabled
choice_c: That the brakes work correctly and the vehicle does not pull to one side
choice_d: That the ABS light illuminates on every stop
explanation: The manual states this procedure is designed to determine that the brakes are working correctly and that the vehicle does not pull to one side.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Service Brake Check

question: What must be checked regarding the safety belt during the in-cab inspection?
choice_a: That it is a certain color
choice_b: That it retracts within two seconds
choice_c: That it has an expiration date printed on the buckle
choice_d: That it is securely mounted, adjusts, latches properly, and is not ripped or frayed
explanation: The manual requires checking that the safety belt is securely mounted, adjusts, latches properly, and is not ripped or frayed.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Safety Belt

question: What must be checked about the steering box during the external inspection?
choice_a: That it is securely mounted, not leaking, and has no missing nuts and/or bolts
choice_b: That it is painted to match the frame
choice_c: That it is replaced every 100,000 miles
choice_d: That it has a warranty sticker attached
explanation: The manual states to check that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking, and to look for missing nuts and/or bolts.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.1 - Steering

question: In addition to the steering box, what else must be checked for leaks or damage?
choice_a: The clutch master cylinder
choice_b: Power steering fluid leaks or damage to power steering hoses
choice_c: The washer fluid reservoir
choice_d: The differential housing
explanation: The manual instructs checking for power steering fluid leaks or damage to power steering hoses.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.1 - Steering

question: What must be checked about the connecting links, arms, and rods from the steering box to the wheel?
choice_a: That they are chrome-plated
choice_b: That they are original manufacturer parts
choice_c: That they are not worn or cracked
choice_d: That they are lubricated hourly
explanation: The manual requires checking that connecting links, arms, and rods from the steering box to the wheel are not worn or cracked.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.1 - Steering Linkage

question: Besides checking that joints and sockets are not worn or loose, what else must be verified about the steering linkage?
choice_a: That it has a manufacturer date stamp
choice_b: That it is insulated from electrical components
choice_c: That it is angled at a specific degree
choice_d: That there are no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys
explanation: The manual states that joints and sockets must not be worn or loose, and there must be no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.1 - Steering Linkage

question: When inspecting leaf springs, what defects should the driver look for?
choice_a: Missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs
choice_b: Excessive shine or polish
choice_c: Mismatched paint color
choice_d: Manufacturer branding wear
explanation: The manual instructs looking for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.2 - Suspension, Springs/Air/Torque

question: What should the driver look for when inspecting coil springs?
choice_a: Overly tight coil spacing
choice_b: Broken or distorted coil springs
choice_c: A missing manufacturer label
choice_d: Coils that are too shiny
explanation: The manual instructs looking for broken or distorted coil springs.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.2 - Suspension, Springs/Air/Torque

question: When inspecting suspension mounts, the driver should look for cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or damaged bushings, and broken, loose, or missing what?
choice_a: Turn signal bulbs
choice_b: Windshield wiper motors
choice_c: Bolts, u-bolts, or other axle mounting parts
choice_d: Fuel injectors
explanation: The manual states to look for broken, loose, or missing bolts, u-bolts, or other axle mounting parts at the mounts.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.2 - Suspension, Mounts

question: What must be verified about the shock absorbers during the external inspection?
choice_a: That they are painted black
choice_b: That they match in brand across all axles
choice_c: That they were installed within the last year
choice_d: That they are secure and have no leaks
explanation: The manual states to see that shock absorbers are secure and that there are no leaks.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.2 - Suspension, Shock Absorbers

question: For manual slack adjustors, how far should the brake pushrod move (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand?
choice_a: No more than one inch
choice_b: No more than six inches
choice_c: No more than three inches
choice_d: It should not move at all, even slightly
explanation: The manual states that for manual slack adjustors, the brake pushrod should not move more than one inch when pulled by hand with the brakes released.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.3 - Brakes, Slack Adjustors and Pushrods

question: What must be checked about the brake chambers?
choice_a: That they are chrome-plated
choice_b: That they are not leaking, cracked, or dented, are mounted securely, and have no loose or missing clamps
choice_c: That they are replaced every oil change
choice_d: That they are labeled with a serial number
explanation: The manual requires checking that brake chambers are not leaking, cracked, or dented, are mounted securely, and have no loose or missing clamps.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.3 - Brakes, Brake Chambers

question: When inspecting a drum brake, what should the driver check for besides cracks, dents, or holes and loose or missing bolts?
choice_a: A recent repaint
choice_b: A manufacturer warranty sticker
choice_c: Contaminates such as debris or oil/grease, and linings not dangerously worn thin
choice_d: An anti-theft locking mechanism
explanation: The manual states to check drum brakes for contaminates such as debris or oil/grease, and that brake linings (where visible) are not dangerously worn thin.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.3 - Brakes, Drum Brake

question: On brake drums with openings that allow the linings to be seen from outside, what must the driver check?
choice_a: That the linings are painted red
choice_b: That the linings are removable without tools
choice_c: That the linings have a visible serial number
choice_d: That a visible amount of brake lining is showing
explanation: The manual states that for this type of drum, the driver must check that a visible amount of brake lining is showing.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.3 - Brakes, Brake Linings

question: What repair is explicitly not allowed on a rim, according to the manual?
choice_a: Welding repairs
choice_b: Sandblasting
choice_c: Repainting
choice_d: Torque wrench tightening
explanation: The manual states that rims cannot have welding repairs.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.4 - Wheels, Rims

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_b: 4/32 inch
choice_c: 6/32 inch
choice_d: 8/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 4/32 inch on steering axle tires.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.4 - Wheels, Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on all tires other than steering axle tires?
choice_a: 4/32 inch
choice_b: 3/32 inch
choice_c: 2/32 inch
choice_d: 1/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 2/32 inch on all other (non-steering axle) tires.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.4 - Wheels, Tires

question: How must the driver check tire inflation to receive credit during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: By visually estimating sidewall bulge
choice_b: By pressing on the tread with a thumb
choice_c: By kicking the tire firmly
choice_d: By using a tire gauge
explanation: The manual states the driver must use a tire gauge and will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.4 - Wheels, Tires

question: What signs might indicate that a lug nut is loose?
choice_a: Rust trails or shiny threads
choice_b: A slightly different paint shade
choice_c: A warm-to-the-touch hub
choice_d: An unusual tire pressure reading
explanation: The manual instructs checking lug nuts for signs of looseness such as rust trails or shiny threads.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.4 - Wheels, Lug Nuts

question: What must be checked about hub oil/grease seals and axle seals, in addition to confirming they are not leaking?
choice_a: That they are a specific brand
choice_b: That, if the wheel has a sight glass, the oil level is adequate
choice_c: That they were replaced within the last month
choice_d: That they make no noise when the wheel spins
explanation: The manual states to see that hub oil/grease seals and axle seals are not leaking and, if the wheel has a sight glass, that the oil level is adequate.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.4 - Wheels, Hub Oil Seals/Axle Seals

question: What must be checked about the fuel tank(s) on the side of the vehicle?
choice_a: That the tank is painted to match the cab
choice_b: That the tank has a locking cap only
choice_c: That tank(s) are secure, cap(s) are tight, and there are no leaks from tank(s) or lines
choice_d: That the tank is mounted above the frame rail
explanation: The manual requires checking that fuel tank(s) are secure, cap(s) are tight, and there are no leaks from tank(s) or lines.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.5 - Side of Vehicle, Fuel Tank

question: What must be checked about the exhaust system?
choice_a: That it is insulated with a heat shield of a specific material
choice_b: That it is painted to prevent rust
choice_c: That it has a manufacturer-approved muffler brand
choice_d: That it is free of damage and signs of leaks, such as rust or carbon soot, and has no cracks, holes, or severe dents
explanation: The manual requires checking the exhaust system for damage and signs of leaks such as rust or carbon soot, with no cracks, holes, or severe dents.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.5 - Side of Vehicle, Exhaust System

question: If equipped, what must be checked about splash guards (mud flaps)?
choice_a: That they are not damaged and are mounted securely
choice_b: That they extend to the ground
choice_c: That they are a specific reflective color
choice_d: That they are removed in winter
explanation: The manual states that, if equipped, splash guards must not be damaged and must be mounted securely.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.6 - Rear of Vehicle, Splash Guards

question: When inspecting the fifth wheel coupling, what must the driver check by looking into the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That the gap is packed with grease
choice_b: That locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin
choice_c: That a warning decal is affixed nearby
choice_d: That the gap is wide enough to insert a hand
explanation: The manual states to look into the fifth wheel gap and check that locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.7 - Tractor/Coupling, Locking Jaws

question: What must be checked regarding the trailer's position on the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: That there is a small visible gap for flexibility
choice_b: That the apron is raised above the skid plate
choice_c: That the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate, with no gap
choice_d: That the kingpin can be seen moving freely
explanation: The manual requires checking that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate, with no gap.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.2.7 - Tractor/Coupling, Kingpin/Apron/Gap

question: In addition to spare fuses, reflective triangles, fusees or flares, and a fire extinguisher, what additional emergency equipment must school bus drivers inspect?
choice_a: A tire chain kit
choice_b: A backup two-way radio
choice_c: A spare tire mounting bracket
choice_d: An Emergency Kit and a Body Fluid Cleanup Kit
explanation: The manual states school bus drivers must also inspect an Emergency Kit and a Body Fluid Cleanup Kit.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.3 - School Bus Only, Emergency Equipment

question: When checking the stop arm on a school bus, what must the driver confirm about its operation?
choice_a: That the stop arm extends fully when operated
choice_b: That the stop arm retracts only when the door is closed
choice_c: That the stop arm is painted a specific shade of red
choice_d: That the stop arm operates independently of the door
explanation: The manual requires checking that the stop arm extends fully when operated.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.3 - School Bus Only, Stop Arm/Safety Arm

question: What must be checked about the trailer's landing gear on the side of the trailer?
choice_a: That it is lowered halfway during transport
choice_b: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged
choice_c: That it is painted a bright color
choice_d: That it is lubricated with grease before every trip
explanation: The manual requires checking that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.4.2 - Side of Trailer, Landing Gear

question: According to the manual, what does the CDL Vehicle Inspection test require in addition to inspecting the entire vehicle?
choice_a: A written essay on brake system theory
choice_b: A demonstration of the alley dock maneuver
choice_c: An engine start, an in-cab inspection, and (for a Class A CDL) an inspection of the coupling system
choice_d: A ride-along with a certified mechanic
explanation: The manual states the Vehicle Inspection requires inspecting the entire vehicle, an engine start, an in-cab inspection, and an inspection of the coupling system if testing for a Class A CDL.
source_note: NM CDL Manual, Section 11.6 - Taking the CDL Vehicle Inspection Test
